raw_case_text:
A 49 year old man presented with chronic headache in 2013, on a background of HIV diagnosed in 1987.
In the early 2000s his CD4+ T cell count was at a lifetime nadir of 70 cells/mul, plasma HIV RNA 5   35 log, and cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) 4   69 log. At that time he had cognitive impairment consistent with HIV associated neurocognitive disorder (HAND) with an MRI brain showing multifocal grey and white matter hyperintensities. CSF was normal including negative PCR for JC virus (JCV) DNA, but a right frontal lobe biopsy showed oligodendrocyte nuclei with viral inclusions, prominent reactive astrocytes including bizarre forms, and was strongly positive for JCV DNA by PCR. HIV associated encephalitis was also present (Anders et al.).
He commenced HAART for the first time with efavirenz, lopinavir/ritonavir, lamivudine, and stavudine (the latter two later switched to raltegravir for tolerability), with consequent CD4+ T cell count rise to over 300 cells/mul. He was clinically stable but required institutional care due to poor cognition that did not improve with HAART.
By 2013 his CD4+ T cell count had been over 500 cells/mul for 7 years, and HIV RNA had been undetectable for a decade. Annual MRI brain scans since 2008 (Figs. 1, 2 and 3) showed progressive white matter atrophy, and since 2010 asymptomatic fluctuating contrast enhancement without mass effect, in both cortical grey and subcortical white matter.
Examination when he presented with headache in 2013 revealed a new right inferior quadrantanopia, preexisting cognitive impairment, mild upper limb action tremor, and impaired tandem gait. CD4+ T cell count was 648 cells/mul. CSF was bland; cryptococcal antigen and HIV RNA were undetectable. However CSF JCV DNA was detected (below 30 copies/mL, the lower limit of quantification of the assay), using primers targeting the VP2 gene. The sequenced 131 base pair PCR product was a 93 % match to JCV CPN1 strain using the Basic Local Alignment Search Tool. MRI brain showed increased subcortical signal hyperintensity and cortical enhancement in the left posterior temporal lobe extending into the parieto-occipital region (Fig. 3). He was diagnosed with possible recurrent PML.
His headache spontaneously improved only to recur several months later. An MRI showed new enhancing lesions in the left temporoparietal grey and subcortical white matter. Serial MR spectroscopic studies showed increasing choline and myoinositol in these regions with markedly reduced N-acetylaspartate implying ongoing gliosis of the subcortical U-fibres. CSF again showed low JC viral load. A stereotactic-guided biopsy of the left temporoparietal lesion was performed within a month of presentation, and repeated six months later because of the unusual findings, with essentially the same result. The patient has shown no clinical progression on history or examination since the biopsies. MRI has not been repeated.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 49-year-old man with a 26-year history of HIV-1 infection and treated progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy (PML) a decade earlier presented in 2013 with recurrent chronic headaches and a right visual field defect.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: Diagnosed with HIV in 1987, the patient had presented in the early 2000s (at nadir CD4 count 70 cells/µL) with cognitive impairment and biopsy-proven right frontal lobe PML and HIV encephalitis; he was started on HAART and achieved CD4+ counts >500 cells/µL for 7 years and undetectable plasma HIV RNA for 10 years, though residual cognitive impairment required institutional care. Annual surveillance brain MRIs since 2010 showed asymptomatic fluctuating cortical and subcortical contrast enhancement, and in 2013 he presented with chronic relapsing headaches.
subjective.past_medical_history: HIV-1 infection diagnosed in 1987 (lifetime nadir CD4+ count 70 cells/µL, baseline plasma HIV RNA 5.35 log10 and CSF HIV RNA 4.69 log10); biopsy-proven right frontal PML and HIV-associated neurocognitive disorder (HAND) / encephalitis in the early 2000s, stably treated with HAART (efavirenz, lopinavir/ritonavir, and raltegravir [switched from lamivudine/stavudine]).
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for chronic relapsing-remitting headache, baseline cognitive impairment, visual field loss, and mild gait unsteadiness. Home medications: efavirenz, lopinavir/ritonavir, and raltegravir.

objective.physical_examination: Neurological examination in 2013 revealed a new right inferior quadrantanopia, baseline cognitive impairment, mild bilateral upper limb action tremor, and impaired tandem gait.
objective.advanced_workup: CD4+ T-cell count in 2013 was 648 cells/µL (maintained >500 cells/µL for 7 years). Lumbar puncture CSF was acellular/bland with undetectable CSF HIV RNA and negative cryptococcal antigen, but ultra-low-level CSF JC virus (JCV) DNA (<30 copies/mL) was amplified using VP2 primers (131-bp product showing 93% sequence identity to the JCV CPN1 strain). Serial brain MRI and MR spectroscopy demonstrated progressive white matter atrophy and new fluctuating cortical grey and subcortical white matter contrast enhancement in the left posterior temporal and parieto-occipital lobes, with elevated choline and myoinositol and markedly reduced N-acetylaspartate indicating active subcortical U-fiber gliosis. Two stereotactic biopsies of the left temporoparietal lesion (performed 6 months apart) confirmed chronic/smoldering inflammatory PML/gliosis.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Late relapsing/smoldering inflammatory progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy (PML) with JCV CPN1-like variant detection (<30 copies/mL in CSF) occurring after 10 years of sustained HIV virological suppression and robust immune reconstitution (CD4+ count 648 cells/µL on efavirenz, lopinavir/ritonavir, and raltegravir). Confirmed by serial CSF VP2 PCR/sequencing, MR spectroscopy, and two stereotactic left temporoparietal brain biopsies; the patient remained clinically stable without neurological progression on continued HAART following the biopsies.
